capture.notes:
The spec is in commit 7149139 ("Visual review capture spec, skipped unless VISUAL_REVIEW=1") on visual-review in /home/claude/hushloom-visual. The file is /home/claude/hushloom-visual/tests/e2e/visual.spec.ts, and typecheck and eslint report nothing on it.

**Runs**
- **Final capture run** on the committed spec: "32 passed (10.1m)", exit 0. The manifest records git.head 7149139 with specDirty false.
- **Earlier run:** a first run also passed 32/32 (9.9m). After it I changed three things: inline-link detection, adding the uncapped smallTargets.groups, and naming the loading shots by route. The final run replaced all of that run's files.
- **Normal suite** ("npx playwright test", VISUAL_REVIEW unset) afterwards: "32 skipped / 36 passed (4.3m)", exit 0. All 32 skipped tests are in visual.spec.ts.

**Output**
- 223 PNGs plus manifest.json in /mnt/project-files/playbox-2/evidence/visual/before/ (68 MB). No fail-*.png was written.
- Each manifest entry has: id, route, url, role, state, width, file, fullPage, HTTP status, checks (h1, overflow, smallTargets, clippedText, contrast) and console errors.
- Captures by role: anonymous 45 + first-visit age gate 3, anonymous in GB 12, member 86, creating member 18, fresh member 27, unverified GB member 18, creator 3, admin 11.

**How the capture works**
- **Setup:** one test creates the data before any capture.
  - The seeded member makes two demo creations (one from a template, one in a project scene), creates the project "Golden hour series" with two scenes, and saves one favorite.
  - There is one template report and one public takedown request.
  - A throwaway account uploads the dev scanner's drill fixture, which creates a real escalation and suspends that account.
  - Four accounts are signed up: fresh, GB, a second GB account, and a "tray" member who is granted 40 credits.
  - Captures run grouped by role, admin first, so the anonymous takedown submissions do not change the admin queue shown at the other widths.
- **Job tray:** after a real confirmed job, page.route freezes the tray's active-list poll at its first non-empty real answer, so the tray stays on screen. The tray entries say this in their note.
- **Loading skeletons:** captured for all 5 loading.tsx routes at every width. Each comes from a real client-side link click, with the non-prefetch RSC request held by page.route.
- **Offline page:** captured through the service worker after context.setOffline(true), plus the offline banner state.
- **Overlays:** sheets and the job tray are viewport-size shots; everything else is full-page.
- **Capture artifact, not a layout bug:** in full-page shots Chromium draws fixed elements where they sit in the first viewport. So the phone tab bar appears at y≈844 over the content, and the desktop rail stops at 900 px. manifest.checks.capture says this.

**Things the captures surfaced for the review round (not fixed here)**
1. **Hydration error on phone (/projects loading shot):** the entry phone-member-projects-loading-skeleton has a page error, "Minified React error #418" (a hydration mismatch). Console errors are logged since the previous capture on that page. In between, the page did a full load of /policies and opened the You sheet. It did not happen in the earlier run, so it looks intermittent.
2. **Signed-out list pages answer 200:** /collection, /favorites and /projects answer 200 with no Location header when requested with maxRedirects 0. The other private pages answer 307 to /auth.
3. **No h1 on the creation detail page:** /collection/<id> has no h1 at any width.
4. **Contrast failure on Pricing:** the "· sandbox" tag inside the Buy button is the only contrast failure found.

The other console errors are expected: the 404 on the not-found page, the 451 when an unverified GB member presses Make it, and ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED plus the RSC fetch fallback while offline.

Not the app's markup, and not the skeleton. It is a React 19.2 hydration bug that the capture's own interception makes frequent. (1) Trigger: the capture's page.route with a predicate makes Playwright intercept every request and turns Chromium's HTTP cache off. Measured: 0/16 JS chunks from cache with the route, 16/16 without. (2) The #418 is thrown while /policies hydrates before the You-sheet click. Server HTML and the client re-render have the same body outline. (3) The stack is rD (throwOnHydrationMismatch) <- oq (beginWork, HostComponent claim) <- iw (replayBeginWork). The unclaimed fiber is the shell's <main> > div.mx-auto, whose children hold an RSC lazy. Next 15.5.27 vendors React 19.2.0-canary-0bdb9206; replayBeginWork there re-claims the host element after the hydration cursor has moved into it. react-dom 19.3.0 resets nextHydratableInstance on replay; 19.2.4 and 19.2.8 do not. (4) It can reach real users: with the cache disabled and no interception, 1 of 130 loads threw. (5) Workaround: the shell passes children through a passthrough PageSlot component, so the suspending fiber is a function component, whose replay leaves the cursor alone. Markup is unchanged. Ten main routes under page.route went from 7/100 to 0/100; the same sweep without a route was 0/100 before.
